label: Jocoque
note: The Mexican kind is a soured milk, traditionally spontaneous, not strained thermophilic yoghurt

about.text: A Mexican fermented milk between yoghurt and cheese, soured with lactic cultures and strained until thick; its dry form, jocoque seco, is eaten with tostadas. It came with Lebanese cooking and resembles labneh.

steps.note: Traditionally soured spontaneously in a clay vessel by a fire with no culture added; today a mix of dairy cultures (species not given) is added to pasteurised milk.
The curd is separated by filtration to firm it.

processing.text: Traditionally no cultures are added; today a mix of dairy cultures (species not given) goes into pasteurised milk. The curd is then strained to firm it.

facts.v: Dehydrated, similar to Arab labneh; 3-4 cm balls may be marinated in olive oil with thyme, dill or mint
